name: Foreground service
plain: Lets the app run long tasks with a visible notification.
meaning: A visible, user-aware background task such as navigation or a call. Types and time limits keep abuse in check.

android.persistence: Not revocable; user can stop from Task Manager
android.store_policy: Play: Foreground service types declaration required for apps targeting 14+; April 2026 preview removes geofencing as approved use effective Aug 26, 2026
android.note: Android 14 requires a type; Android 15 dataSync and mediaProcessing limited to about 6 hours in 24; starting from background restricted since Android 12.

ios.store_policy: App Review 2.5.4: background modes only for relevant features
ios.note: iOS limits background execution to defined modes; iOS 26 adds user-initiated continued processing.

limits.headline: Can run long tasks on Android with a visible notification, but only for a stated purpose
limits.user_action: You start something long, like a download, a workout or a file sync
can: Keep a long task going while the app is closed, with a notification showing
Declare a type such as media, location or data sync, as Android 14 requires
Use a new user started task on iPhone in iOS 26
cannot: Run a data sync or media processing service past about 6 hours in 24 on Android 15
Start one from the background in many cases; Android restricts that
Run freely on iPhone, which allows only set background modes
limits.differs: Android has foreground services with a notification. iPhone limits background work to set modes, plus user started processing in iOS 26.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app run a long task in the background while showing a visible notification.

marketing.name: Foreground services
marketing.pitch: Google describes foreground services as work the user is aware of, shown with a notification.

story.for_you: You see a notification while an app is doing something long, like navigating or recording. It is the sign the app is allowed to keep going.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for calls, navigation and fitness. Android requires a type and limits time so it is not a hiding place.

use_cases.example: A navigation app keeps giving directions with the screen off.
A run tracker keeps recording your route while you check messages.
A call keeps going after you leave the app.
A player keeps playing in your pocket.
A game download or a cloud stream continues while you do something else.
A security app keeps a camera feed ready for alerts.
A screen recorder keeps capturing a live stream.

story.android_note: Android 14 needs a type. Android 15 limits data sync to about 6 hours in 24.
story.ios_note: iOS only allows background modes. iOS 26 adds user started continued processing.

linkedin.how: Exodus snippets show FOREGROUND_SERVICE (4.1.637) and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE (4.1.995) in the LinkedIn manifest. What feature drives it is not documented; voice recording in messages is the likely driver (inferred).

history.change: Time limits for dataSync and mediaProcessing
Foreground service types and matching permissions required
Typed foreground services required with matching permission
Foreground services cannot be started from background with exceptions
